result:
Compilation succeeded (the deprecation note is expected since the tests exercise `applyRules` and the deprecated `format(Object, StringBuffer, FieldPosition)` overload).

I created `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java`, covering:
- Constructor null-argument checks (`NullPointerException` for pattern/timeZone/locale)
- Getters (`getPattern`, `getTimeZone`, `getLocale`)
- `format` for `long`, `Date`, `Calendar`, into `String`/`StringBuffer`/generic `Appendable`, including padding rules, literal quoted text, weekday/month names, and RFC822/ISO8601 time zone offsets
- The documented Calendar-vs-printer time zone interaction
- Package-private `format(Object)` for `Date`/`Calendar`/`Long`
- Deprecated `format(Object, StringBuffer, FieldPosition)` and `applyRules`
- `getMaxLengthEstimate` positivity, determinism, and the "actual length ≤ estimate" bound across boundary dates
- `equals`/`hashCode` contract (reflexive, null/foreign-type, equivalence, and differences in pattern/timeZone/locale)
- `toString` non-null/non-empty
- Distinctness of `FULL`/`LONG`/`MEDIUM`/`SHORT`
- `parsePattern` (non-empty, empty-pattern, and invalid unterminated-quote boundary case)
- `selectNumberRule` non-null returns
- Static `getTimeZoneDisplay` cross-checked against `TimeZone.getDisplayName`, and `clear()` not breaking subsequent lookups

No other files were modified.
